THIS INVOCATION closed the last open clause, 'no sensitive graph material is durably cached', by BUILDING the behavior and proving it at two tiers rather than rewording the row. Choke-point design: privacy.go is the single definition of CacheControlPrivateNoStore = 'private, no-store', and the two graph response writers writeJSON (success) and WriteError (every typed error; WriteAPIError and GraphCapability.WriteDisabled funnel through it) stamp it, so every family, list and detail, success and error and the disabled 503, is covered without editing a handler and a newly added family inherits the contract automatically. Ordering is load-bearing: SetPrivateNoStore MUST precede WriteHeader because Go freezes the header map at the status line, so a later Set is silently dropped with no compile or runtime error; two of the three adversarial privacy_test.go unit tests exist specifically to fail if that ordering is inverted. TIER SPLIT: the unit tests prove the writers SET the header before commit but, observing only a ResponseRecorder, cannot prove it survives; the live run proves it SURVIVES the full middleware chain to the wire - ./smackerel.sh test e2e --go-run 'TestE2E_GraphResponsesArePrivateNoStore|TestE2E_GraphFamilyJourneyIsReadOnly|TestE2E_ExpiredSessionAndDeniedScope' (2026-07-28T08:31:42Z -> 08:35:39Z, ===PRIVACY_E2E_EXIT=0===): graph-owned 200 detail, 200 list, and 400 typed error each carry EXACTLY 'private, no-store', all 8 canonical manifest paths are no-store-bearing, and the pre-handler 401 carries the global bare 'no-store' from securityHeadersMiddleware.
